entry.title: The Internet’s Full of Trash Info, So I Made Nexix. You’re Welcome 💅
entry.summary:
You ever search something online and end up reading a novel about someone’s traumatic backstory with JavaScript just to find the answer in paragraph 47? Same.
So I said screw that — and I built my own thing.
Introducing: Nexix. It’s like ChatGPT, Google, and Wikipedia had a baby… but then that baby said “nah, I’m built different.” Nexix is an AI-powered platform that answers your questions fast, clean, and with no fluff.
No SEO clickbait. No 5-minute intros. Just facts, clarity, and boom—you’re smarter. And yes, it works on your phone. No, you don’t need to download anything. And YES, it’s free.
Because your brain deserves better than fighting through ad-ridden blog jungles. I was tired of “how to center a div” turning into a TED Talk about CSS history.
I wanted to learn fast, not read war and peace every time I had a question. And most AI tools? Either too slow, too generic, or trying too hard to sound like Shakespeare with a laptop. So I made Nexix: ✨ Beautiful glassmorphic UI (dark theme, blue accents, chef’s kiss) 🧠 Answers generated instantly by AI (via Groq, so it’s F A S T) Students tired of searching the same crap over and over Indie devs like me who hate wasting time Curious minds who want answers, not clickbait People who value their time over someone’s recipe blog from 2014 👉 [https://nexix.netlify.app]
Just search something. Anything.
You'll either learn something, or get addicted to how fast it is. Either way, W. Drop 'em. Roast it. Praise it. Tell your friends.
This isn’t a startup. This is a movement 💪 Let’s kill slow learning together.
– Liemar 💻

entry.title: How to Set Up a Static Backend IP for Cloud Run Revision using VPC Connector
entry.summary:
When deploying services on Cloud Run, the default behaviour is that the backend IP address (that is, where requests to external endpoints come from within your app), is assigned from a dynamic IP address pool. Therefore, for cases that require IP whitelisting, you need to configure the Cloud Run instance to use a static backend IP, which can be achieved through the magic✨ (read: networking capabilities) of VPC Connector. Note that we are referring to the outbound IP here, not the inbound IP which instead is how traffic gets to our Cloud Run instance and can be configured via a load balancer. Check out the Google Cloud docs here for static outbound IP addresses
gcloud compute routers create my-router --network=default --region=my-region Creating router [my-router]...done. NAME …
